questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 62°. What is the alternate angle on the other line?
questions.why: Alternate angles sit on opposite sides of the transversal between the parallel lines and are always equal, so the answer is 62°, not the co-interior supplement 118°.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: What did Magna Carta say the king had to do before punishing a free man?
questions.why: Magna Carta 1215 established that even the king was bound by the law and could not punish free men without lawful judgment, limiting royal power.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has one angle of 110° and no equal sides. What type of triangle is it?
questions.why: An angle over 90° makes a triangle obtuse, and no equal sides makes it scalene, so it is an obtuse scalene triangle.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Which religion held Jerusalem as a holy city, alongside Christianity and Judaism, during the Crusades?
questions.why: Jerusalem was sacred to Christians, Jews, and Muslims alike, which is why control of the city was so fiercely contested during the Crusades.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Black Death killed huge numbers of workers. What was a long-term consequence of this labour shortage?
questions.why: The mass deaths (cause) meant fewer workers were left, so survivors could demand higher wages (consequence). The other options are earlier causes or unrelated events, not results of the labour shortage.
options: Trade routes brought the plague to England

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: Which of these best shows globalisation increasing interconnection?
questions.why: Global supply chains link countries through trade and production, showing how globalisation connects economies worldwide, unlike purely local activities.

questions.subject: English
questions.why: Romeo and Juliet was written by William Shakespeare in the 1590s, one of his earliest tragedies.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: A student tests whether the amount of water given affects plant height, keeping pot size the same for all plants. What is the independent variable?
questions.why: The independent variable is the one the scientist deliberately changes — here, the amount of water. Plant height is measured (dependent), and pot size is kept the same (controlled).

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: What poetic form do Romeo and Juliet speak in when they first meet at the party?
questions.why: Shakespeare has Romeo and Juliet share a sonnet at their first meeting, its formal rhyme scheme signalling their instant romantic connection.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: In sexual reproduction, offspring get genetic material from how many parents?
questions.why: Sexual reproduction combines genetic material from two parents, creating genetic variation, unlike asexual reproduction where offspring come from one parent.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 105°. What is the co-interior angle on the other line?
questions.why: Co-interior (allied) angles sum to 180° because they lie between the parallel lines on the same side, so 180° minus 105° gives 75°.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: Your classmate says: 'In an experiment testing whether the volume of music affects how fast a person reads, the number of pages read is the independent variable, since that's what changes most.' Using an example of your own, explain what actually makes a variable independent, dependent, or controlled, and correct your classmate's mistake.
